coverage.description: Optional transparency block. Not part of the PS floor — shows what was actually checked, including where evidence was insufficient or degraded, so the audit can honestly say 'not enough evidence' instead of manufacturing a finding.

self_compliance_checked.description: Evidence that the audit tool itself respected robots.txt for its own fetches — distinct from bot_policy_analysis, which is about the site's policy toward other crawlers. One entry per path the tool considered fetching.

fetched.description: false if allowed was false and the tool correctly skipped it.

opportunities.description: Optional. Proactive, non-obvious improvements that would strengthen discoverability or engagement even where no explicit defect was found — the PS explicitly invites suggestions that go beyond detected problems. Distinct from findings[]: these never carry a severity because they are not a diagnosed problem.

rationale.description: One line on the mechanism this would help with. Must not assert a specific unverified fact about the site (a figure, a named integration, a count) — keep this to the general mechanism. Any specific site fact the rationale depends on belongs in the sibling 'evidence' field instead, so it carries the same grounding as a finding.

evidence.description: Optional, but required if 'rationale' or 'summary' states a specific fact that was actually observed on the site (e.g. 'the site already publishes X at /path') rather than a generic recommendation. Same plain-string, evidence-state-backed discipline as findings[].evidence — do not state an unverified specific fact (a named integration, a precise count) without this field backing it.

confidence.description: Optional. Certainty of the underlying evidence, kept separate from severity — see severity-rules.md.

check_id.description: Optional internal mechanism id, e.g. 'fact-cross-representation'. Never a research citation.

affected_scope.description: Optional. See scope-and-time.md. Report language must match this scope.

why_it_matters.description: Optional one-line mechanism explanation, in plain language, without overclaiming a downstream guarantee.

evidence.description: Required, plain string, matching the PS floor exactly (e.g. 'Crawled 3 sampled pages; price present in rendered DOM, not observed in raw HTTP, metadata, or structured data on 1/3.'). Richer structured detail lives in the sibling 'evidence_detail' field below — this field itself must stay a human-readable sentence, not an object.

evidence_detail.description: Optional. Structured detail behind the 'evidence' sentence above — additive, never a replacement for it.

evidence_state.description: The controlled-vocabulary state(s) from evidence-states.md that this finding was reconciled from.

fetch_status.description: Optional. Whether the underlying page fetch succeeded. This build has a single fetch mechanism (the invoking agent's native fetch tool) — see evidence-states.md — so there is no per-observation fetch-method distinction to record anymore, only whether the fetch itself succeeded. Never describe an observation using rendered-DOM language regardless of this value.
